disclaimer: Deadlines encoded from public regulatory texts for demonstration. Not legal advice; every obligation must be confirmed by counsel. Items marked 'verify' have known ambiguity or recent amendments.

regulations.name: EU General Data Protection Regulation
regulations.regulator: Lead supervisory authority (e.g. Irish Data Protection Commission)

stages.label: Notify supervisory authority
stages.wording: without undue delay and, where feasible, not later than 72 hours after having become aware of it
stages.plain: Tell the data-protection regulator within 72 hours of becoming aware of a personal-data breach. Late notifications must explain the delay.
stages.waivable: Only if the breach is unlikely to result in a risk to people's rights and freedoms (Art. 33(1)); the decision must still be documented (Art. 33(5)).

stages.label: Notify affected individuals
stages.plain: If the breach is likely to cause HIGH risk to people, tell them directly, in clear language, without undue delay.
stages.noFixedDeadline: Without undue delay (no fixed hour count)

regulations.name: EU Digital Operational Resilience Act
regulations.regulator: National competent authority (e.g. Central Bank of Ireland / ECB for significant banks)

stages.label: Initial notification
stages.citation: DORA Art. 19(4)(a); Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2025/301 Art. 5
stages.wording: within 4 hours from classification as major, and no later than 24 hours from becoming aware of the incident
stages.plain: Once an incident is classed as MAJOR, send an initial notice within 4 hours, but never later than 24 hours after you first detected it.

stages.label: Intermediate report
stages.wording: within 72 hours from the submission of the initial notification
stages.plain: Follow up with more detail within 72 hours of sending the initial notice.

stages.label: Final report
stages.wording: within one month from the latest updated intermediate report
stages.plain: A full final report including root cause, within one month of the intermediate report.

regulations.name: CERT-In Directions under IT Act s.70B(6)

stages.label: Report to CERT-In
stages.wording: within 6 hours of noticing such incidents or being brought to notice about such incidents
stages.plain: Report listed cyber incidents (data breaches, ransomware, unauthorised access…) to CERT-In within 6 hours of noticing them.

regulations.name: RBI cyber incident reporting for banks
regulations.verify: RBI's 2016 Cyber Security Framework said 2–6 hours; the 2023 IT Governance Master Direction says 6 hours. Confirm the current circular.

stages.label: Report to RBI
stages.citation: RBI Master Direction on IT Governance, Risk, Controls & Assurance Practices (7 Nov 2023); Cyber Security Framework in Banks (2 Jun 2016)
stages.plain: Banks regulated by the Reserve Bank of India must report cyber incidents within 6 hours of detecting them.

regulations.name: India Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023 & Rules 2025
regulations.verify: Timelines from the DPDP Rules 2025 (Rule 7); phased commencement, so confirm they are in force for this entity.

stages.label: Intimate Board & affected people
stages.citation: DPDP Act 2023 s.8(6); DPDP Rules 2025 Rule 7(1)–(2)(a)
stages.plain: Tell the Data Protection Board and every affected person without delay: what happened, the likely impact, and what they can do.

stages.label: Detailed report to Board
stages.wording: within 72 hours of becoming aware of the breach, or such longer period as the Board may allow
stages.plain: Send the Board a detailed report (facts, cause, mitigation, people notified) within 72 hours of becoming aware.

regulations.name: NYDFS Cybersecurity Regulation (23 NYCRR 500)
regulations.regulator: New York State Department of Financial Services

stages.label: Notify DFS of cybersecurity incident
stages.wording: as promptly as possible but in no event later than 72 hours after determining that a cybersecurity incident has occurred
stages.plain: Notify New York's financial regulator within 72 hours of determining a reportable incident occurred.

stages.label: Notice of extortion payment
stages.wording: within 24 hours of the extortion payment
stages.plain: If a ransom is paid, notify DFS within 24 hours, and explain why within 30 days.

regulations.name: SEC cybersecurity incident disclosure
regulations.verify: Counts weekdays only; US federal holidays and the 5:30pm ET filing cut-off are not modelled.

stages.label: File Form 8-K Item 1.05
stages.wording: within four business days after the registrant determines that a cybersecurity incident is material
stages.plain: Public disclosure within 4 BUSINESS days of deciding the incident is material to investors. Weekends don't count.
